- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot peaks, especially when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.4).
- Underestimate early in the horizon when sentiment is weak or negative (sentiment < 0.3), leading to lagged corrections.
- Mean-reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after strong upward moves, especially if sentiment is high but recent.
- When sentiment is rising (positive trend), model tends to overreact; when sentiment is falling, it underreacts — adjust forecast slope downward with falling sentiment.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid assuming momentum; if last 3–5 days show volatility, reduce forecast variance and favor mid-range values.
- If sentiment is consistently above 0.5 over last 5 days, reduce forecast growth rate by 10–15% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3–5 days, model may be overfitting recent trends — apply downward bias correction for next forecast.
